options.B: The presence of vector organisms required to carry the pathogen across rooms
options.C: The size of the respiratory particles and how long they remain suspended in the air
options.D: The specific anatomical portal of entry where the pathogen invades the host body

explanation: Large droplets drop quickly within a short distance, whereas tiny airborne nuclei stay afloat and drift across considerable distances. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary target of luteinizing hormone in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Sertoli cells
options.B: Leydig cells
options.C: Prostate cells
options.D: Spermatids

explanation: Luteinizing hormone binds to receptors on the interstitial Leydig cells to stimulate the synthesis and secretion of testosterone. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T6#GNS121_U4_T6_h3)

question: How does community mobilisation differ from a traditional top-down health delivery model?

options.A: It treats community members as active partners rather than passive recipients
options.B: It eliminates the need for formal healthcare facilities in rural areas
options.C: It focuses only on curative medicine instead of preventive health
options.D: It relies exclusively on international funding rather than local resources

explanation: The participatory approach ensures that the community is involved from the planning stage rather than simply receiving directives from health authorities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the correct positioning for an unconscious, breathing adult patient to maintain an open airway?

options.A: Supine position with flat headrest
options.B: Trendelenburg position with tilted pelvis
options.C: Upright sitting position at 90 degrees
options.D: Recovery position on their side

explanation: The lateral recovery position prevents the tongue from falling back against the pharynx and allows fluids or vomitus to drain safely from the mouth. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is a referral necessary when a client requests a long-acting reversible contraceptive requiring surgical insertion at a basic health post?

options.A: National guidelines strictly forbid any contraceptive procedures outside tertiary hospitals
options.B: The required service exceeds the technical capacity of the initial point of contact
options.C: Basic health posts completely lack trained female healthcare personnel
options.D: Clients must pay an extra penalty fee for advanced procedures

explanation: When specialized skills or equipment are missing at a primary site, clients must be moved to facilities equipped to handle those specific procedures safely. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a strict cold chain for vaccines?

options.A: To accelerate the absorption rate of the antigen into the muscle
options.B: To preserve the potency and effectiveness of the biological product
options.C: To make the injection less painful when administered to the infant
options.D: To prevent the physical vials from melting in tropical climates

explanation: Vaccines are sensitive biological substances that degrade and lose efficacy if exposed to improper temperatures outside the cold chain range. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h4)
